Article Title: Jasprit Bumrah and the rest: The familiar storyline replays at Basin Reserve
Article Text:
Jasprit Bumrah (Photo by BCCI)

WELLINGTON: Minutes after Devdutt Padikkal dropped a regulation catch off centurion Henry Nicholls , Rishabh Pant, with his hands behind his back, stared at the replay on the giant screen. Pant was distraught after losing the opportunity to break the Nicholls-Glenn Phillips partnership, summing up India's day. The body language became flatter, and the players dragged themselves around the field, waiting for the umpires to call it a day.The unbeaten 173-run stand allowed the hosts to stage an emphatic fightback and exposed vulnerabilities in India's inexperienced bowling attack. Jasprit Bumrah was relentless from one end, but containing the batters became difficult after the pitch lost its initial spice and the moisture evaporated under the harsh sun. There was a light shower before the Indian team arrived at the venue, but Wild Welly was on snooze mode as conditions remained very pleasant after that.There were no gusts of wind or dark grey clouds, and while India did come hard with the new ball, they allowed the advantage to slip away with some lacklustre bowling in the post-lunch session. Bumrah, on either side of the break, set the game up nicely but didn't get support from the other end.The ghosts of the Manchester Test were back haunting Anshul Kamboj as the Haryana fast bowler lost his zip and speed as the game progressed. Akash Deep was impressive but didn't get the rub of the green as he bowled much better than the figures suggest.The biggest letdown of the day was Prasidh Krishna's manner of operation. India are obsessed with tall fast bowlers who can hit the deck hard, but Prasidh lacked penetration and control during his 16-over spell. Plenty of comfortable half-trackers were dispatched with disdain, continuing the familiar storyline of Bumrah and the rest at the Basin Reserve.Playing his first Test since the home Test against South Africa last year, Bumrah was on the money from the word go. It took the bowler just three deliveries to draw first blood, and he was very sharp, beating both edges of the batters. There was encouraging seam movement for the bowler, and he rarely missed his mark, consistently finding the ideal good-length spot.His seven-over spell, two before lunch and five after, was in unplayable territory as he asked many questions. The set-up for Darryl Mitchell, which included a short-leg fielder and consistently targeted the stumps, worked because the right-hander kept walking towards the deliveries to negate the movement. Result: Bat-pad to Yashasvi Jaiswal, who took a sharp catch.Tom Blundell came in against an on-song Bumrah and survived only 22 deliveries before nicking one to Shubman Gill. At 70/5, India were one wicket away from entering the New Zealand lower order, but the moment never arrived. For the next 322 deliveries, Gill changed his bowlers, swapped their ends, even took the new ball when it became available close to stumps, but nothing worked.There was no option but to bowl spin from one end to keep the over-rate in check, which further allowed the Nicholls-Phillips stand to grow in confidence and flourish. When they return to the field on Day 2 of the Test, India would hope they can replicate the morning session from the opening day and will again pin their hopes on that man Bumrah.New Zealand: 243 for 5 after 83 overs (Henry Nicholls 113 not out, Glenn Philips 94; Jasprit Bumrah 3/52)
Article Summary: Jasprit Bumrah was relentless from one end, but containing the batters became difficult after the pitch lost its initial spice. Prasidh Krishna lacked penetration and control during his 16-over spell. The ghosts of the Manchester Test were back haunting Anshul Kamboj as the Haryana fast bowler lost his zip and speed as the game progressed.

Article Title: Why Mohammed Siraj's absence from Wellington Test is harsh but not a surprise
Article Text:

WELLINGTON: Mohammed Siraj was the most trending keyword as India stepped onto the field for the first Test against New Zealand. His omission from the series opener triggered a massive debate. While it's harsh on the proven match-winner, it doesn't come as a surprise. The sequence of events, starting with the one-off Test against Afghanistan, dropped enough cues about the team management's thinking.Siraj was asked to play the game with little turnaround time following the IPL 2026 final his team, Gujarat Titans (GT), played. He wasn't considered for ODI cricket, which followed, with Shubman Gill making it clear that the team prefers tall fast bowlers who can operate at pace. With no game time under his belt, Siraj boarded the flight to Sri Lanka for the two-Test series, and insufficient bowling volume was reflected in his rhythm during the Galle Test.His pace and penetration dropped drastically, leading to discussions about playing Gurnoor Brar for the Colombo Test. A late change of heart kept the experienced bowler in the playing XI for the second Test, but his returns were again underwhelming as Sri Lanka denied India a much-needed win. This takes nothing away from his ability to win matches for the country, but it forced the management to start exploring options.When the selectors, coach and captain discussed the bowling group for the New Zealand Tests, Siraj remained in the mix, but there was renewed excitement around Akash Deep regaining fitness. The likes of Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi also joined the discussion because of their batting abilities. Siraj, meanwhile, was building his red-ball volume with outings in the Duleep Trophy and Ranji Trophy.The selectors dropped the next cue when they made him play just one India A game in New Zealand, keeping him with the ODI squad while the other Test bowlers, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj, were released for red-ball preparations. Siraj remained on the bench even in ODIs as late entrant Auqib Nabi, who replaced Prasidh Krishna in the squad, played ahead of him. It was only after Gurnoor Brar was added to the Test squad and released before the fifth ODI that Siraj played only his fifth ODI of the year.Before the first Test, Gill reiterated that they were looking at batting contributions from their bowlers at No. 8 and No. 9 and emphasised his preference for tall fast bowlers. The message was clear: they need bowlers with high pace to keep them in play during different phases of the Test.When asked about Siraj's exclusion, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak asserted that they played the XI the management felt best suited for these conditions. Kotak further added that Siraj remains world-class and said there was nothing wrong with the bowler that led to his omission from the Wellington Test.“There is nothing wrong. I mean, I can't see anything wrong,” Kotak told reporters after the day's play. “That's the best possible XI the team management thought, and that is the one which played. Sri Lanka, obviously, it was different conditions, and Siraj played both the Tests there.”Whether it's the right or wrong call is not the discussion right now; the focus should be on why the management's actions over the last few months and the build-up to this Test made his exclusion unsurprising.
Article Summary: Mohammed Siraj was the most trending keyword as India stepped onto the field for the first Test against New Zealand. His omission from the series opener triggered a massive debate. The sequence of events, starting with the one-off Test against Afghanistan, dropped enough cues about the team management's thinking.

Article Title: Infantino remains favourite as FIFA president gets two challengers for 2027 vote
Article Text:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino, left, Kohzo Tashima, and Philippe Diallo. (AP Photo)

UEFA-backed Diallo emerges as key challenger

Infantino remains favourite despite eligibility questions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FIFA president Gianni Infantino will face his first contested re-election battle since 2023, with French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo and Japan's Kozo Tashima emerging as challengers for the top job at world football's governing body.Both candidates submitted their nominations ahead of the midnight deadline in Zurich, with letters of support from five member federations, FIFA confirmed on Thursday. The election involving FIFA's 211 member associations is scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat, Morocco.Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, was re-elected unopposed in 2023. He is now seeking another four-year term, which would keep him in office until 2031 and take his presidency to 15 years."The candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidates," FIFA said in a statement.The governing body added: "Member associations will be notified of the names of the proposed and admitted candidates no later than 18 February 2027."Diallo announced his candidacy on Monday with the backing of UEFA member associations represented on its executive committee and the FIFA Council.He took over as FFF president in 2023 and played a leading role in the European opposition to Infantino's FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.Tashima had declared his intention to contest the election earlier this month and formally submitted his nomination on Wednesday.The FFE proposal, which sought to sell private investors stakes in the profits of the World Cup and other major competitions, triggered a fierce backlash after it was revealed in July. Infantino eventually dropped the plan."Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of FIFA, the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community," UEFA said on Monday.Despite repeated calls for his resignation, Infantino is widely seen as the favourite, with many of FIFA's member associations outside Europe appearing satisfied with his leadership. He has directed significant funding towards national federations and promised an additional $25 million to each through 2030.However, his bid for another term could face scrutiny over FIFA's presidential term limits. The statutes allow three full terms, but FIFA's legal advice in 2022 held that Infantino's initial 2016-19 stint, when he completed Sepp Blatter's unfinished mandate, did not count towards the limit.Candidates must also pass eligibility and integrity checks by FIFA's three-member electoral panel, whose decisions can be challenged at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.The final list of approved candidates is due by February 18, 2027.
Article Summary: UEFA-backed Diallo emerges as key challenger for FIFA presidency. FIFA president Gianni Infantino will face his first contested re-election battle since 2023. French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo and Japan's Kozo Tashima emerge as challengers for the top job.

Article Title: '140 clicks was hard to come by': Ravi Shastri questions India's pace attack, asks 'Where was Siraj?'
Article Text:
Mohammed Siraj (AP Photo)

India batting coach defends Siraj's omission

India vs New Zealand, 1st Test: Day 1 report

Former India head coach Ravi Shastri questioned India's decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the opening Test against New Zealand, after the hosts staged a remarkable recovery on Day 1 at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday.India appeared to have seized control of the contest after reducing New Zealand to 70/5, with Jasprit Bumrah leading the charge. However, Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips produced a stunning counterattack, stitching together an unbeaten 173-run partnership to take the hosts to 243/5 at stumps.With India's pace attack struggling to make further inroads after the initial breakthroughs, Siraj's omission became a major talking point among former cricketers and experts.Taking to X after the day's play, Shastri questioned whether India's selection committee had overlooked the experience and aggression that the Hyderabad pacer brings to the bowling attack."Hope India bounce back strongly. But if pace, skill and seam movement were the criteria, and 140 clicks was hard to come by, one has to ask the question. Where was MOHD SIRAJ? Experience, aggression and the ability to make things happen with the ball.Surely that counts for something!" Shastri wrote.Meanwhile, India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defended the team management's decision, insisting that the playing XI was selected keeping the entire five-day contest in mind rather than just the opening day.Kotak maintained that there was nothing wrong with Siraj and backed the combination chosen for the Wellington Test."There is nothing wrong with Siraj. We thought this was the best XI when we picked the side. I don't think dropping Siraj was a wrong decision. This is just the first day. We don't pick a team only for day one, but also for days two, three and four," Kotak said.Earlier in the day, India enjoyed a commanding start after winning the toss and opting to bowl. Bumrah struck with the third delivery of the match, dismissing New Zealand captain Tom Latham for a duck. The visitors continued to exploit the early assistance on offer, with Akash Deep and Bumrah among the wickets as New Zealand struggled to negotiate the movement and bounce.Rachin Ravindra and Daryl Mitchell also departed cheaply, while Bumrah removed Tom Blundell shortly after lunch to leave the hosts reeling at 70/5. However, Nicholls and Phillips turned the contest around with a magnificent partnership. Nicholls remained unbeaten on 113 off 221 deliveries, striking 14 boundaries, while Phillips finished the day on 94 not out off 182 balls, with 13 fours.The duo added 173 runs without being separated, taking New Zealand to 243/5 after 82 overs at stumps on Day 1.Bumrah was India's standout bowler with three wickets, while Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj picked up one apiece. Prasidh Krishna, however, went wicketless as the hosts wrested back control of the contest.With Phillips just six runs short of his century and Nicholls well-set at the other end, India will need early breakthroughs on Day 2 to prevent New Zealand from building a substantial first-innings total.
Article Summary: India bowler Jasprit Bumrah took three wickets on Day 1. Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips added 173 runs to take New Zealand to 243/5. Ravi Shastri questioned India's decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI. India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defended the team management's decision.

Aresilient Bihar on Wednesday showed that they can win without Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, defeating a star-studded Delhi side by two wickets in the last over of their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Group B match in Indore. Chasing 225, Bihar reached 227/8 in 19.5 overs with the ninth wicket pair of Mayank Kumar (24*, 13b, 3x6) and Prashant Singh (13*, 8b, 2x4) adding 37 in 20 balls. Sooryavanshi was missing from the Bihar side as he is on India ‘A’ duty for ACC Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026.After being asked to bat first, Delhi posted 224/5 in 20 overs, thanks to Yash Dhull’s brilliant 59-ball 125 (16x4, 7x6). Bihar began the chase in fifth gear, racing away to 96 in Powerplay. Wicketkeeper-batter Ayush Loharuka led the charge with a knock of 50 (22b; 7x4, 3x6), putting on 92 runs with No. 3 batter Bipin Saurabh (49 off 19b, 3x4, 5x6) in just 31 balls for the second wicket. However, Delhi fought back through their spinners but Mayank and Prashant turned the game around with their partnership.: Delhi 224/5 in 20 overs (Dhull 125, Dahiya 51; Raghavendra 3-44) lost to Bihar 227-8 in 19.5 overs (Loharuka 50, Bipin Saurabh 49, Mayank 24 not out; Digvesh Rathi 3-47) by 2 wickets.Asuperb display by Sairaj Patil (40 off 21 and 3/27 in three overs) helped Mumbai beat Goa by 18 runs to record their third straight win. Electing to bat first, Mumbai put up 207 in 18.5 overs, even though no batter scored a half-century. Goa were reduced to 23/3 in the third over before Lalit Yadav (81, 41b, 14x4, 1x6) and Deeraj Gaonkar added 72 for the fourth wicket in 48 balls to bring them back in the game. A spirited Goa eventually finished with 189 in 19 overs.: Mumbai 207 in 18.5 overs (Musheer 44) beat Goa 189 in 19 overs (Lalit 81, Deepraj 48; Sairaj 3-27) by 18 runs.Leg-spinner Yuzvendra Chahal , who picked up 3/16 in four overs against Tamil Nadu in Indore on Wednesday, achieved a big milestone when he became the first Indian bowler to take 400 T20 wickets. The 36-year-old reached the feat when he clean bowled Tamil Nadu opener Amit Sathvik. Among Indians, Bhuvneshwar Kumar (366) & Jasprit Bumrah (354) are next highest T20 wicket-takers.Skipper Abhimanyu Easwaran struck an unbeaten 61 while Abishek Porel contributed 49 as Bengal chased down Jharkhand’s 148/7 to register a seven-wicket victory.: Jharkhand 148-7 in 20 overs (Virat 45, Shikhar 42; Sayan 2-23, Rishabh 2-31) lost to Bengal 149-3 in 18.4 overs (Easwaran 61, Porel 49) by 7 wickets.
Article Summary: Yuzvendra Chahal becomes first Indian bowler to take 400 T20 wickets. Bihar beat Delhi by two wickets in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Group B match. Mumbai beat Goa by 18 runs to record their third straight win.

NEW DELHI: Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson lost his patience at a press conference after being repeatedly questioned about Babar Azam ’s poor form and whether fans should be concerned ahead of next year’s World Cup.Hesson defended the star batter and made it clear that he wanted journalists to focus more on Pakistan’s performance against Sri Lanka rather than repeatedly discussing Babar.The questions came after Babar scored 92 runs in three innings during the ongoing Test series against Sri Lanka. Article Title: Gautam Gambhir's Kiwi Test: A defining red-ball challenge awaits India head coach in New Zealand
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir and Shubman Gill (AFP Photo)

Few opponents have shaped Gautam Gambhir ’s cricketing journey quite like New Zealand. It was an ODI series in India vs the Black Caps in 20102011 where he first became India captain as MS Dhoni and Virender Sehwag were rested.It was against the Kiwis that he announced himself as one of India’s finest Test openers during the 2008-09 tour, scoring 445 runs in three Tests at an average of 89. His 137 and the 10-hour, 43-minute vigil in Napier in the second innings remains one of the most celebrated rescue acts by an Indian batter overseas and a masterclass in defensive batting that helped save a Test match and laid the foundation for a historic series victory.More than 15 years later, New Zealand continue to occupy a special place in Gambhir’s cricketing story, though not always for pleasant reasons. The Kiwis handed him the most embarrassing setback of his coaching tenure when they whitewashed India 3-0 at home in 2024, the first such defeat on Indian soil. Yet they were also the opponents India overcame in the Champions Trophy final in Dubai in 2025 and again in the T20 World Cup final earlier this year in Ahmedabad, victories that strengthened Gambhir’s reputation as a white-ball coach.On this sojourn, he has overseen series wins against New Zealand in both limited-overs formats. But Test cricket, the format Gambhir cherishes most, presents a completely different examination.The stakes could hardly be higher. India need victories in both Tests to remain firmly in contention for a place in the 2027 World Test Championship final.Having already missed out on the previous cycle’s final despite appearing favourites when Gambhir succeeded Rahul Dravid, another failure would inevitably raise uncomfortable questions about his red-ball credentials. That is where New Zealand present both a challenge and an opportunity.While Gambhir’s preference for multi-skilled cricketers has served India well in T20 cricket, the same philosophy has not always delivered in Tests.On more than one occasion, particularly overseas, India have appeared caught between strengthening the batting and maximising wickettaking options. Such hedging has robbed the side of the firepower needed to own the decisive moments.Team selection, therefore, could prove as important as execution.Communication between Gambhir and bowling coach Morne Morkel has been constant since the latter left the white-ball squad after the rain-hit ODI in Hamilton and travelled to Wellington to oversee preparations for the Test series.Asked about the attack at India’s disposal, Morkel’s message to the head coach was definitive.“My feedback to Gautam was that we have enough in attack to take 20 wickets.”That belief could shape India’s selections over the next two weeks.Despite being one of the architects of India’s T20 revolution through the 2007 World Cup triumph, Gambhir remains deeply old-school in his cricketing outlook.In an era when youngsters romanticise about an IPL gig more than an India cap, he continues to view Ranji Trophy as the ideal finishing school and Test cricket as the ultimate dipstick to measure a player and team’s worth. It is a philosophy he has repeatedly articulated.Success in the longest format, he believes, leaves the deepest imprint and defines legacies. New Zealand now offers him the chance to reinforce that belief.
Article Summary: Gautam Gambhir has overseen series wins against New Zealand in both limited- overs formats. But Test cricket presents a completely different examination. The stakes could hardly be higher. India need victories in both Tests to remain firmly in contention for a place in the 2027 World Test Championship final.

Article Title: Inspired by Sunelita, Pooja Sahoo eyes dream debut as India begin ACT campaign
Article Text:
Pooja Sahoo

“I want to make it there too.”That was the thought that crossed Pooja Sahoo’s mind when fellow villager Sunelita Toppo broke into the Indian women’s hockey team as a teenager.Several years and countless training sessions later, the defender from Kukuda village in Odisha’s Sundargarh district has earned a maiden senior call-up of her own after being named in India’s squad for the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy, which begins in Bhopal on Thursday with the hosts taking on Malaysia in the opening match.For the 19-year-old, the selection is the culmination of a journey that began by watching players from the region and dreaming of following in their footsteps. “I started playing hockey when I was around 13 or 14 years old. There were many players around me and watching them play inspired me to take up the sport,” Pooja told TOI.Among those who inspired her was Sunelita, who had made the Indian team at the age of 16. “When she got her opportunity at such a young age, I felt that I wanted to reach that level too. My only goal was to make it to the senior team one day,” Pooja said.That ambition carried her through years in the junior setup. After progressing through Odisha’s hockey pathway, she trained at STC Centre in Sundargarh before moving to the National Centre of Excellence in New Delhi. She subsequently became a regular in the junior national programme, featuring on India’s Europe tour, playing in the Junior World Cup and helping the team win the Junior Women’s Asia Cup earlier this year.Pooja credits much of her growth to the experiences she gained in national camps and from learning under different coaches. One aspect of her game that has particularly impressed coaches is her drag-flicking ability. She first learnt the basics of drag-flicking under coach Pradeep Sarangi in Sundargarh before refining the skill during her time in Bengaluru and closely observing Harmanpreet Singh.The defender also believes her stint in the Hockey India League accelerated her development. Representing Shrachi Bengal Tigers, she had the opportunity to play alongside and learn from foreign stars, including Argentine drag-flick specialist Agustina Gorzelany. “It was a great experience playing with Gorzelany. She would often guide me and give me advice about different aspects of my game,” said Pooja.Known among her coaches for her vocal presence on the field, Pooja said communication came naturally to her. “I just enjoy expressing myself, sharing what I know and helping others. Communicating with teammates is something I enjoy,” she said.Now, with her first senior international tournament beckoning, Pooja is focussed on giving her absolute best. “I want to use everything I have learnt over the years and contribute as much as possible to the team’s success,” she added.She will get the chance to do exactly that on Thursday when Sjoerd Marijne-coached India open their campaign against Malaysia. Fresh from their Asian Games gold-medal triumph, the hosts will start as one of the favourites for the title, though Asian Games silver medallists China are expected to provide the sternest challenge despite the departure of coach Alyson Annan after more than four years in charge.Today’s matches: China vs Thailand, Japan vs South Korea, India vs Malaysia.
Article Summary: Pooja Sahoo has been named in India's squad for the Women's Asian Champions Trophy, which begins in Bhopal on Thursday. The 19-year-old defender from Kukuda village in Odisha’s Sundargarh district has earned a maiden senior call-up.

Article Title: Premier League champions Leicester City cut ties with sponsor after porn actress appointment sparks fan backlash
Article Text:
Leicester City have parted ways with their sponsor after the firm appointed a porn actress as an ambassador.

Fans question Leicester's association with gambling and pornography

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From Premier League champions to League One

Leicester City have parted ways with front-of-shirt sponsor BC Game after the gambling firm's appointment of Russian porn actress Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador triggered a backlash from supporters of the former Premier League champions.The League One club announced on Wednesday that the commercial partnership, which began at the start of the 2024-25 season, had been terminated with immediate effect following discussions between the two parties."Leicester City Football Club and BC.GAME have reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect," the club said in a statement. "The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward."BC Game announced Elfie as its brand ambassador earlier this month, posting a promotional video featuring the Russian adult film actor and a delivery driver on social media with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin."The appointment drew criticism from Leicester supporters, with the Foxes Trust Supporters Group questioning the club's association with a gambling company that had now brought pornography into its brand promotions.The supporters' group had expressed its opposition to the sponsorship arrangement even before the latest development, arguing that both gambling and pornography could have harmful consequences, particularly for young people."From the moment the club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company, we felt Leicester City were ditching its values," the Foxes Trust said in a statement on November 4. "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City."Is this who we are now?"The club's decision to end the partnership comes after the growing criticism surrounding BC Game's choice of ambassador. Leicester also confirmed an enhanced returns policy for supporters who had purchased shirts carrying the sponsor's branding.Under the arrangement, fans who bought BC Game-branded shirts since October 21 can seek an exchange or refund, even if the shirts have been worn or personalised.The club also thanked BC Game for the "constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement".The sponsorship controversy comes during a difficult period for Leicester, whose remarkable Premier League triumph in the 2015-16 season remains one of English football's most celebrated underdog stories.Having defied the odds to lift the title, the Midlands club have since endured a dramatic decline, suffering back-to-back relegations and dropping into the third tier of English football.The end of the BC Game association marks another significant off-field development for a club seeking to rebuild its fortunes.
Article Summary: Leicester City have parted ways with front-of-shirt sponsor BC Game. The gambling firm's appointment of Russian porn actress Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador triggered a backlash from supporters of the former Premier League champions. Leicester also confirmed an enhanced returns policy for supporters who had purchased shirts carrying the sponsor's branding.

Article Title: Retired at 25, inducted at 30! Ash Barty admits 'imposter syndrome' ahead of Hall of Fame honour
Article Text:
Australia's Ash Barty (AP Photo)

Three Grand Slams, 114 weeks at No. 1

'It was always never': No comeback plans

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ash Barty's tennis career ended at just 25, barely two months after winning the 2022 Australian Open. Five years later, the three-time Grand Slam champion is set to join the sport's immortals, but the former world No. 1 is still struggling to come to terms with the honour.Barty, now 30, has been elected to the International Tennis Hall of Fame (ITHF) and will be formally inducted at a ceremony in Newport, Rhode Island, next August. Yet, true to her understated nature, the Australian admitted she feels a little uncomfortable being placed alongside the absolute legends of the game."I feel very, very humbled and grateful. And to be honest, I've got a little bit of impostor syndrome where I feel I don't quite belong," Barty told Reuters. "The Hall of Fame is for the absolute legends of our game, and I'm not sure I'm quite there."The surprise announcement was made during a call with ITHF co-presidents Kim Clijsters and Patrick McEnroe. Barty was also touched by personal congratulatory messages from nearly 20 Hall of Famers, including Roger Federer and Martina Navratilova Barty's achievements, however, leave little doubt about her place among tennis greats. She won three Grand Slam singles titles on three different surfaces, lifting the French Open in 2019, Wimbledon in 2021 and the Australian Open in 2022.Her Melbourne triumph ended Australia's 44-year wait for a homegrown women's singles champion. She also spent 114 consecutive weeks at the top of the world rankings.The Australian will be inducted alongside Japan's Shingo Kunieda, a four-time Paralympic gold medallist and 50-time major champion, who has been elected in the wheelchair tennis category.Barty said the recognition was as much for the people who supported her through her career as it was for her."I'm probably most excited to tell my team because it feels like it's as much for me as it is for them," she said.Her journey was far from straightforward, featuring struggles with depression, a nearly two-year break from tennis and a spell as a professional cricketer before she returned to the sport.Barty's retirement at 25, soon after the biggest triumph of her career, has repeatedly fuelled speculation about a possible comeback. But the Australian, now a mother of two, made it clear that she has no intention of returning to professional tennis.Asked whether her position had shifted from "never say never" to simply "never", she replied: "No, mate, it was always never."She also insisted she had no regrets about walking away from the sport at the peak of her powers."No, no, no, not one."Barty said she was fully immersed in family life and that her children were still unaware of her tennis achievements."My kids don't even know that I played tennis, and I'm sure that at the induction next year they'll wonder what's going on," she said. "I'm deep in the trenches with my two little ones at the moment, and I absolutely love it."Barty will become the second Indigenous Australian inducted into the Hall of Fame, after Evonne Goolagong Cawley, and hopes her recognition can inspire future generations."I think if you can provide the opportunity and the platform for them to learn and grow, then hopefully, maybe one day, there's another young boy or girl being inducted into the Hall of Fame," she said.
Article Summary: Ash Barty has been elected to the International Tennis Hall of Fame. The 30-year-old will be formally inducted at a ceremony in Newport, Rhode Island, next August. The three-time Grand Slam champion is set to join the sport's immortals. Barty says she feels a little uncomfortable being placed alongside the legends of the game.

Article Title: India clinch historic lawn bowls series in New Zealand
Article Text:
(From left) Dinesh Kumar, Reshma Kumari, Pinki Singh and Sunil Bahadur after winning the trophy in Auckland on Wednesday

India completed a remarkable turnaround to clinch the three-match lawn bowls series against New Zealand with a 3-2 victory in the deciding test at Royal Oak Bowls in Auckland on Wednesday.Having lost the opening test before levelling the series with a comeback win on Tuesday, the Indian team produced another composed performance to seal the trophy on New Zealand soil.The experienced Jharkhand duo of Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur gave India a winning start, defeating their New Zealand opponents 9-7 in the men’s pairs. New Zealand hit back in the women’s pairs, where Reshma Kumari and Pinki Singh went down 2-5.India regained the advantage in the mixed fours as the quartet grabbed a crucial 7-5 victory. The visitors then sealed the overall test by winning the first mixed pairs contest 5-2. Although New Zealand claimed the second mixed pairs match 7-4, India had already secured an unassailable lead and with it the test and the series.The triumph completed a stunning recovery after India lost the opening test and found themselves adapting to unfamiliar conditions in Auckland. According to Dinesh, belief in their own abilities proved crucial to the turnaround.“We know that if we play our natural game, we can challenge any team in the world. We showed that here. We kept reminding each other to play our best and leave everything on the green. Everyone gave their all, and we achieved our goal,” he said on Wednesday.For Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki, the key to India’s revival lay in the unity shown by the four-member contingent. “The best thing was our unity. None of us made excuses about being tired, lacking sleep or facing difficult conditions. All four of us played as one team. We fought together, came back together and eventually won the series together,” Pinki said.Sunil, meanwhile, underlined the significance of winning the trophy away from home.“The biggest satisfaction comes from winning on New Zealand’s home turf. Winning in India would have been special, but coming here, competing in their conditions and taking the trophy back home makes the achievement even more meaningful,” he said.The series victory provides another significant boost for Indian lawn bowls in what has already been a successful year for the sport and will serve as a confidence booster ahead of upcoming international competitions, including the World Championships.
Article Summary: India complete remarkable turnaround to clinch three-match lawn bowls series against New Zealand with a 3-2 victory in the deciding test at Royal Oak Bowls in Auckland on Wednesday. The triumph completed a stunning recovery after India lost the opening test and found themselves adapting to unfamiliar conditions in Auckland.

Article Title: Venugopal Rao: 'Built a cricket ecosystem from scratch, now ready for the next chapter'
Article Text:
Venugopal Rao, Delhi Capitals former director of cricket. speaks to Sameer Rizvi after a net session during the IPL 2025 at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi. (ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Former India cricketer Venugopal Rao says he is "happy" and "content" when asked what's next for him after ending his four-and-a-half-year association with GMR Group 's cricket franchises, where he served as Director of Cricket."I am in Hyderabad, enjoying my time away from cricket. Now I'm taking some time out to be with my family. My kids have also been asking for my time, so that's important," Rao tells TimesofIndia.com.The 44-year-old has been the architect of the GMR Group's cricketing operations across the globe. He played a pivotal role in guiding Dubai Capitals to the ILT20 title in 2025 and was appointed Delhi Capitals' Director of Cricket for the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons. He also joined Seattle Orcas as General Manager of Cricket Operations and has helped steady the ship at Southern Brave in The Hundred, a franchise in which the GMR Group has invested heavily."For four-and-a-half years, I was involved day in and day out, setting up the entire system. When I came in, nothing was in place. I built the whole cricket ecosystem, brought people in, and they did well," he says."But I will definitely get involved with teams and do something in cricket again. I can't keep myself away from the game for too long. For the next four or five months, I'll take some time and see what happens. I'm looking forward to opportunities and will see where things go," adds Rao, a veteran of 121 first-class matches.Under Venugopal Rao and head coach Hemang Badani, the Delhi-based franchise finished fifth and sixth in IPL 2025 and 2026, respectively. Sourav Ganguly has now been appointed as Delhi Capitals' head coach ahead of IPL 2027. The move follows the agreement reached between DC co-owners GMR Sports India Pvt Ltd and JSW Sports, under which the two partners would alternate control of the franchise's operations in two-year cycles.“When you look back at our first season (IPL 2025), especially the two games against Mumbai Indians, one at home and one away, I think we could have won both. In the first game in Delhi, we had four or five run-outs, which cost us the match. Karun played a superb knock, and we could have chased the target comfortably. Even in the Mumbai game, we had four or five run-outs, which again cost us," Rao reflects."In the Mumbai game, Axar Patel missed out due to illness. If you look at the surface, it was turning, and Mitchell Santner was a crucial bowler for them who picked up an important wicket. Axar was a big miss for us, not just with the ball but also while batting. As a left-hander, he would have been better equipped to tackle left-arm spin."Those were the two games in our first season that we missed out on, and winning them could have helped us qualify for the knockouts."Rao feels that even in the second season, in 2026, they were in contention for the playoff spots and could have qualified with a bit of luck."Even in the second season, if you look back at the home game against Gujarat Titans, David Miller was on strike. We needed two runs off two balls, but we couldn't win the game. That was our biggest disappointment. A player like Miller should have finished that game," he says."There was also the game against Punjab in which we scored 265. A lot of people say we should have defended that total, but if you look at the circumstances, Lungi Ngidi got injured and had to go to the hospital. That cost us around four hours. At the same time, we dropped eight catches."Normally, if you score 265 and drop eight catches, it's difficult to defend that total. If we had won those two games, Gujarat would have finished in the top two. That's how the IPL works, and we had to accept it," he adds.On the debate over whether Axar Patel or KL Rahul should lead Delhi Capitals (DC), Rao believes the incoming leadership should be allowed to operate without interference.“Whoever takes over should be given a free hand. Whether it’s Axar or KL, both have played at this level and understand the game. I have always believed in giving people freedom. Mistakes can happen, but your intentions should be good. If they are, you should have the clarity and freedom to take decisions," he says.Rao cites KL Rahul's turnaround as an example. After a slow start in IPL 2024, Rahul finished as the franchise's leading run-scorer, amassing 539 runs that season and 593 in IPL 2025."We backed KL Rahul and gave him a particular role. From the first season to the second, we worked on building his confidence. We told him he would have our support, and that was important. He delivered. He told us that if we backed him, he would deliver the results, and he did," he says.Rao also stressed that backing the coaching staff and management is central to building a successful franchise. Citing Chennai Super Kings' turnaround after a difficult 2020 season and RCB's consistency in reaching the playoffs before winning the title in 2025, he said teams needed to trust their cricketing personnel and allow them to work."The difference between teams that win championships and those that don't is often the support staff, the processes and the freedom given to people. Miracles may happen occasionally, but consistency is what helps teams win trophies and matches. Look at teams like CSK, Mumbai Indians and Kolkata Knight Riders. When the management gives people a free hand, it makes a difference."I still remember Chennai Super Kings having a difficult season in 2020. They didn't finish in the top four, but from what I heard from MS Dhoni, he maintained the same atmosphere in the dressing room and didn't allow outside interference. The following season, they won the trophy."You can see something similar with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB). The hard work over three years helped them consistently qualify for the playoffs. When I spoke to Faf du Plessis, who was with us at DC, he told me that the cricketing decisions were largely left to the cricketers.The management was involved, but the cricketing people had the freedom to do their job."In franchise cricket, you often see the difference when the people responsible for cricket are allowed to take decisions. There is a lot of noise on social media, with people asking teams to change this or that. But if you keep interfering, the franchise will always struggle to build consistency," he adds.
Article Summary: Former India cricketer Venugopal Rao says he is "happy" and "content" when asked what's next for him after ending his four-and-a-half-year association with GMR Group's cricket franchises. He played a pivotal role in guiding Dubai Capitals to the ILT20 title in 2025 and was appointed Delhi Capitals' Director of Cricket for the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons. He also joined Seattle Orcas as General Manager of Cricket Operations.

Article Title: 'We want to get as many runs as possible': Nicholls eyes more frustration for India after stunning recovery
Article Text:
Henry Nicholls (AFP Photo)

Nicholls eyes bigger total, warns of India's fresh bowling attack

Nicholls praises Phillips' counterattacking approach

Nicholls, Phillips frustrate India with unbeaten 173-run stand

New Zealand turned the opening day of the first Test against India on its head with a remarkable fightback led by Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips , who rescued the hosts from a precarious position to put them in the driver's seat at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday. After India reduced New Zealand to 70/5, the duo combined resilience with counterattacking strokeplay to take the hosts to 243/5 at stumps, leaving the visitors with plenty of work to do on Day 2.Nicholls, who brought up a magnificent century, remained unbeaten on 113 off 221 deliveries, while Phillips was closing in on his hundred at 94 not out. The pair stitched together an unbeaten 173-run stand for the sixth wicket, completely shifting the momentum in New Zealand's favour.Speaking after the conclusion of Day 1, Nicholls stressed the importance of carrying the momentum into the second morning, insisting that the partnership must be extended and the first-innings total pushed as high as possible.Reflecting on the team's recovery, Nicholls expressed satisfaction at reaching stumps without losing another wicket but acknowledged that the challenge was far from over. He emphasised the need to remain focused, particularly with India's bowlers expected to return with renewed energy on Day 2.“We want to get as many runs as possible. Considering where we were earlier and where we are now, it's pleasing that Glenn and I have managed to remain unbeaten overnight. However, we know we have to put in the hard work again tomorrow. The Indian bowlers will come back fresh in the morning, and our priority will be to build on this partnership and take the total as high as possible," Nicholls told reporters after Day 1.The left-handed batter also reserved special praise for his batting partner, highlighting Phillips' aggressive approach and ability to keep the Indian bowlers under pressure.“Glenn is great to bat with. The way he counterattacks and runs between the wickets puts tremendous pressure on the bowlers. We complement each other well because we are both very busy at the crease. When you have someone at the other end who is constantly looking to put the bowlers under pressure, it makes your job a little easier."He's also quite entertaining, as you might have heard on the stump mic, with some of his reactions to deliveries. He's a valuable part of our batting line-up, and his approach is quite different, as we saw from the very beginning today," he added.The fifth-wicket breakthrough had initially put India in complete control, with New Zealand struggling at 70/5. However, Nicholls displayed tremendous patience and discipline to anchor the innings, remaining unbeaten on 113 off 221 balls, including 14 boundaries.Phillips, meanwhile, brought a different dimension to the partnership. The right-hander remained unbeaten on 94 off 182 deliveries, striking 13 boundaries and ensuring that the Indian bowlers could not settle into a rhythm.Their 173-run unbroken partnership off 322 deliveries not only prevented a potential collapse but also transformed what had been India's dominant day into a promising one for the hosts.
Article Summary: New Zealand reach 243/5 at stumps on Day 1 of the first Test against India. Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips stitched together an unbeaten 173-run stand for the sixth wicket. Nicholls remained unbeaten on 113 off 221 deliveries, while Phillips was closing in on his hundred.

Article Title: 'Cummins will struggle to captain Australia': Ian Healy's blunt warning after Bancroft's Sandpapergate revelations
Article Text:
Cameron Bancroft and Pat Cummins

Healy calls for Lehmann to speak, rules out fresh probe

Former Australia wicketkeeper Ian Healy has warned that Pat Cummins will struggle to lead the Test side unless he directly refutes Cameron Bancroft ’s explosive claim that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering plan during the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test.Bancroft, one of the central figures in the Sandpapergate scandal, said on Tuesday that the entire team was aware of the conspiracy but he ended up taking "the bullet" for everyone. His remarks have reignited questions over what happened in South Africa and the credibility of those who maintained they knew nothing about the plot.The latest controversy follows Cummins dismissing former teammate Usman Khawaja 's claim in his book that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering plan as “complete and utter nonsense.”Reacting to Bancroft's fresh allegations, Healy said Cummins needed to address the issue directly if he wanted to retain his authority as captain."I would feel without refuting Cameron Bancroft's words again, he (Cummins) will struggle to captain the team.“You've had a big part of your credibility taken away with that press conference now that it's been proven to be not as complete as Pat made it out to be,” Healy told SEN.Asked whether Cummins should stand down as Australia captain, Healy said he did not believe that was necessary, while questioning the way Cricket Australia had handled the scandal in 2018."No, he doesn't need to stand down. And I don't want to get into another panic mode of what happened in 2018, it was panic, and they tried to do an investigation in no time, didn't talk to anyone, it was rubbish. It was a lack of quality and rubbish, and rushed, and panicked."Now, I can't say whether he should stand down now. Will he stand down? That might be a different thing. He might stand down," said the 62-year-old, who played 119 Tests and 168 ODIs between 1988 and 1999.Healy also argued that the latest revelations could damage the personal legacies of Cummins and fellow Australia bowlers Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, who had said they were unaware of the ball-tampering plan.“I would say it taints their personal legacies. I don't think it's going to taint their performance legacies. Personally now, they're not as credible as they once were, unless they change something drastically in the next few days," Healy said.Healy also suggested that the ball-tampering could have been happening for longer than previously believed.“So they probably achieved some success with their skills, with a ball that's doing more than it was going to. That's a little bit of a part of their career legacy," he added.Healy believes former Australia coach Darren Lehmann should now disclose what he knows about the scandal."If he's going to do it, now's the time. But I think the dots have been joined there too. It was an ugly underbelly with an average attitude, and he was in charge of it,” Healy said.Healy also accused Cricket Australia of orchestrating a cover-up in the aftermath of the scandal, arguing that the panic following the events in South Africa resulted in a flawed investigation.“Yes, I think so...the panic and the chaos back here in Australia - they had no idea about it in South Africa - it was unbelievably emotional and led to a poor quality investigation which might have been covering up a motivation not to get everyone sacked," he said.However, Healy does not believe Cricket Australia should reopen the investigation.“No. I don't think there's any value in it. The dots are joining for us now. So I’m saying no. It would be costly, it would be ugly, and continuing something that should have been better handled the first time, but it could be wrapped up quite well without spending a whole lot of money, I reckon,” he added.
Article Summary: Former Australia wicketkeeper Ian Healy has warned that Pat Cummins will struggle to lead the Test side unless he directly refutes Cameron Bancroft’s explosive claim that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering plan during the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test. Healy said Cummins needed to address the issue directly if he wanted to retain his authority as captain.

NEW DELHI: Just when India needed a breakthrough to break New Zealand's growing partnership, they missed a big chance in the first Test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday. Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips had put together a partnership of more than 150 runs and were making life difficult for the Indian bowlers. However, India got an opportunity to break the stand in the 74th over when Nicholls mistimed a pull shot off Prasidh Krishna.The ball went high in the air towards backward square leg, where Devdutt Padikkal was waiting. But wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant also ran towards the ball, leading to confusion between the two fielders.Padikkal initially hesitated as Pant came into his line of sight. Pant also slowed down before realising that Padikkal was better placed to take the catch. By the time Padikkal stretched his hands, it was too late. He got his fingertips to the ball but could not hold on.Prasidh was left in disbelief and covered his mouth with his hand. Padikkal and Pant also looked disappointed, while India captain Shubman Gill was visibly unhappy with the missed chance.It was a costly miss for India as Nicholls got another opportunity to continue his innings and New Zealand's fightback.India had started well after Gill won the toss and elected to bowl. Jasprit Bumrah and Anshul Kamboj reduced New Zealand to 12/2 early in the innings.Bumrah dismissed New Zealand captain Tom Latham for a duck, while Kamboj sent back Devon Conway for four.Henry Nicholls and Rachin Ravindra then tried to steady the innings and took the hosts to 50 in 18.2 overs. However, Akash Deep broke the partnership in the following over by dismissing Ravindra for 15.Bumrah struck again just before lunch, removing Daryl Mitchell for one. He then dismissed wicketkeeper-batter Tom Blundell for five in the second session.Bumrah had three wickets to his name, while Kamboj and Akash Deep picked up one each.New Zealand were struggling at 70/5 at one stage, but Nicholls and Phillips fought back with a big partnership. The hosts reached 232/5 after 78 overs, putting India under pressure.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

Third Paralympics, one big dream: Gold at LA 2028

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.
Article Summary: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The Indian shuttler lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23- 21, 8-21, 15-21. Suhas has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.China topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze.Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. She also extended her congratulations to the entire Indian contingent.Para athletics was India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Para badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze.India also won 11 medals in para swimming, seven in para table tennis, six in para archery and five in para shooting. The contingent added two medals each in para judo and para powerlifting.The closing ceremony brought together athletes, officials and dignitaries to mark the conclusion of the Games. Asian Paralympic Committee president Majid Rashed declared the event closed, highlighting the growing strength of para sport across Asia and its role in building a more inclusive society.Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also praised the athletes' determination, teamwork and sportsmanship, describing their performances as a reminder of the “profound beauty” of para sports.The Asian Para Games began in Guangzhou, China, in 2010, evolving from the Far East and South Pacific Games Federation for the Disabled. The Aichi-Nagoya edition was the fifth staging of the event, with Doha, Qatar, scheduled to host the sixth in 2030.For India, the closing ceremony marked the end of a historic campaign — one that raised the country's medal benchmark and showcased the depth and growing strength of its para-sport movement.

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.

Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan

Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
