Article Title: Former Real Madrid legend Gareth Bale partners with $1bn American investment firm exploring €500 million takeover of one of Spain's biggest and oldest clubs in bidding war against Saudi investors
Article Text:
Gareth Bale targets Sevilla ownership, joining forces with American investors to pursue a €500m takeover of Spanish football’s seven-time Europa League champions.

Gareth Bale linked with investment group interested in buying Sevilla

El Confidencial

Why Sevilla need investment after years of sporting decline

Bale's Cardiff City takeover attempt and his ambitions beyond football

Front Office Sports

Wales skipper Gareth Bale promised to play on for the country after they were knocked out of the FIFA World Cup in the group stage after losing 3-0 vs England, as per Reuters.

Who else is competing to acquire Sevilla?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gareth Bale could be preparing for an unexpected return to Spanish football, although this time his ambitions extend beyond the pitch. The former Real Madrid and Tottenham forward is reportedly advising an American investment group interested in acquiring Sevilla, the seven-time Europa League winners who have endured several difficult seasons. With the club seeking fresh investment and multiple parties considering bids, Bale’s latest move could bring him closer to the football ownership ambitions he has discussed since retiring.According to Spanish publication, Juggernaut Capital Partners is among the investment groups exploring a potential takeover of Sevilla, with Bale reportedly involved in an advisory capacity. The Welshman is not understood to be leading the proposed acquisition personally, but his association with the American fund places him within a group considering an investment in one of Spanish football’s most recognisable clubs.The Washington DC-based private equity firm manages more than $1 billion in investor capital and was founded in 2009. Bale joined forces with the company and its managing partner, John Shulman, in June 2026, when they launched Juggernaut Diversified Sports, a dedicated platform focused on sports investment. The new sports fund has a target below $1 billion, distinguishing its intended fundraising from the larger pool of capital managed by Juggernaut Capital Partners.The firm already has experience in the sports industry, having backed KemperSports, a golf course management company, and Thrill Sports, a Las Vegas-based business involved in action sports and combat entertainment. Bale also has an existing investment in TGL, the technology-driven indoor golf league founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, giving him commercial interests beyond his former football career.Sevilla are available for acquisition as the club seeks investment following several seasons of financial losses. Investment bank Goldman Sachs is reportedly overseeing a process involving the potential sale of up to 85 per cent of the club’s shares, with a valuation of approximately €500 million, equivalent to around £417 million. Bidders have reportedly been given until mid-December 2026 to submit proposals, with a takeover potentially completed in early 2027.Sevilla's appeal to potential investors is difficult to separate from the contrast between their European achievements and recent domestic struggles. The Andalusian club have won the Europa League seven times, more than any other side, establishing a reputation for performing particularly well in the competition despite frequently operating outside Spain's traditional title contenders.Their recent league performances, however, have been considerably less convincing. Sevilla have failed to finish in the top half of La Liga in each of the previous four seasons, while their 2024-25 campaign brought them dangerously close to relegation. They finished that season just one point above the relegation zone, a position far removed from the club's standing during its most successful European campaigns.The situation has not improved sufficiently during the current campaign, with Sevilla sitting 13th in La Liga ahead of their forthcoming Seville derby against Real Betis. Their need for fresh capital extends beyond improving the first-team squad, particularly given the financial losses that have prompted the current sale process.The club's European history nevertheless gives potential investors an established identity and considerable commercial recognition. Sevilla have built a particularly strong relationship with the Europa League, winning the competition seven times and developing a record that remains unmatched by any other club. Their challenge is restoring the consistency required to compete more regularly near the top of Spanish football, rather than relying on their European reputation alone.The reported Sevilla interest follows Bale's unsuccessful attempts to acquire his boyhood club, Cardiff City, during 2025. Two formal takeover bids were launched, but the club's owner, Vincent Tan, ultimately declined to sell, preventing the former Wales captain from completing a return to the team he supported growing up.Bale subsequently made clear that the failed Cardiff discussions had not ended his interest in football ownership. Speaking toin June 2026, after the launch of Juggernaut Diversified Sports, he explained that finding the appropriate investment opportunity remained more important than rushing into an acquisition.“It's about being patient, finding the right club, and the right path for us to take. That doesn't mean Cardiff is off the table. But I think now we have a bit of time and will look around.”His involvement with Juggernaut provides a potential route into ownership through an established investment operation, rather than requiring him to finance an acquisition independently. Bale has an estimated personal fortune of approximately £120 million, accumulated through his playing career, endorsements and investments, although his reported role in the Sevilla discussions remains advisory.During his career, Bale scored 226 goals in 664 appearances for club and country before announcing his retirement in January 2023, aged 33. He spent the final three years of his playing career in Major League Soccer with Los Angeles FC, having previously represented Tottenham, Real Madrid and Southampton. His career also included five Champions League titles with Real Madrid and a central role in Wales reaching the semi-finals of Euro 2016.Juggernaut Capital Partners are not the only potential investors examining the opportunity, with two other groups reportedly interested in acquiring shares in Sevilla. One is HD Ventures, an investment group led by Saudi brothers Mansour Sayed and Haidar Sayed, who are understood to be pursuing a rival proposal.The other is a local Seville consortium led by Antonio Lappi and Federico Quintero, whose involvement would offer a potential alternative to the international investment groups. The presence of several interested parties could complicate negotiations, particularly with the club's valuation and the proposed shareholding structure still central to any agreement.Sevilla have also been linked with another former Real Madrid player, Sergio Ramos, who previously pursued a controlling investment in the club alongside a consortium. However, that proposed transaction fell through in late May 2026, with reports suggesting disagreements emerged after the terms of the deal changed during negotiations.
Article Summary: Gareth Bale is reportedly advising an American investment group interested in acquiring Sevilla. The seven-time Europa League winners are seeking investment following several seasons of financial losses. Goldman Sachs is reportedly overseeing the potential sale of up to 85 per cent of the club’s shares, with a valuation of approximately €500 million, equivalent to around £417 million.

Article Title: 'Thanks football': World Cup, Champions League winner Juan Mata announces retirement at 38 after glittering career
Article Text:
File Pic: Former Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata. (Reuters Photo)

From Spain's golden generation to European glory

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Trophy-winning journey continued after England

Former Spain, Chelsea and Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 38 on Wednesday, bringing the curtain down on a distinguished career that featured some of the biggest honours in the game.The Spaniard, who won the FIFA World Cup, the UEFA European Championship and the UEFA Champions League , confirmed his decision through a video posted on social media, recorded in the dressing room at Juventud Estadio in Oviedo, where he began playing organised football at the age of 10."Sometimes, to love is to let go... Thanks football," Mata wrote in his post.His retirement comes after a successful final stint in Australia's A-League with Melbourne Victory, where he enjoyed an impressive 2025-26 campaign. He scored five goals and provided 13 assists, earning the Johnny Warren Medal as the league's best player. He also won the best playmaker award.Mata was part of Spain's golden generation that dominated international football between 2008 and 2012. He was a member of the squad that won the 2010 World Cup in South Africa, where Spain defeated the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time.Two years later, he scored in Spain's 4-0 victory over Italy in the Euro 2012 final, helping the country retain its continental crown.He finished his international career with 41 appearances and 10 goals.At club level, Mata began his journey in Real Madrid's youth academy before making his breakthrough at Valencia, where he won the Copa del Rey in 2008.His move to Chelsea in 2011 marked another defining chapter. In his first season at Stamford Bridge, he helped the London club win the Champions League in 2012, defeating Bayern Munich in the final. He also lifted the FA Cup in 2012 and the Europa League in 2013.Mata joined Manchester United in January 2014 and spent around eight-and-a-half years at Old Trafford, making 285 appearances. His honours included the FA Cup in 2016, the Europa League in 2017, the League Cup and the Community Shield.After leaving England in 2022, Mata continued adding silverware to his collection. He won the Turkish league title with Galatasaray in the 2022-23 season before helping Japan's Vissel Kobe secure the J.League crown in 2023.He subsequently moved to Australia, playing for Melbourne Victory and Western Sydney Wanderers. Following his departure from Victory in September, he committed to an ownership interest in the club and took on the role of chair of its football committee.Beyond his achievements on the pitch, Mata also co-founded Common Goal in 2017, an initiative encouraging footballers to pledge one per cent of their income towards community projects and social change.With his retirement, one of the most decorated midfielders of Spain's golden era brings an end to a career spanning nearly two decades and multiple continents.
Article Summary: Juan Mata has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 38. The Spaniard won the FIFA World Cup, the UEFA European Championship and the UEFA Champions League during a distinguished career. His retirement comes after a successful final stint in Australia's A-League with Melbourne Victory.

Article Title: Moosa’s faith turns India’s underdogs into champions
Article Text:
Sandip Mandi’s last-gasp goal helped India clinch 10th straight title

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Panaji: India coach Naushad Moosa was tired of his squad being described as “depleted” at every media interaction in Bangladesh, but his response never really changed.“I told everyone that I trust my boys, they will do well, and they will win the competition,” Moosa told TOI over a video call from his hotel room in Dhaka. “I had strong belief in this team because many of them had played for me before (in the under-23 team). If I don’t believe in my players, they will never be convinced. Countries came with their best teams, many had overseas players, but I knew that our players are better. They only needed an opportunity to perform and prove themselves.”Nobody really gave Moosa and the India team a chance at the SAFF Championship.India had a “depleted” squad with the seniors being handpicked for two friendlies in New Zealand. Players checked in and left in quick time. When Moosa sought reinforcements for the final, nobody helped.Yet, against the odds, India defeated arch-rivals Pakistan 2-1 in the final. The sending off of Junaid Shah crippled the opponents but Moosa believed India had the momentum on their side and would have found a way past a side that had six players based in Europe.“I didn’t have to say anything in the dressing room (at half time).The players said we are surely winning this one. I just reminded them that they are being too nice (on the field). In the first half, Pakistan were hitting us, elbowing, and we could not continue like this. We had to show our nasty side. In the second half, we had control. We were killing them with crosses. The red card helped us too,” said Moosa.India’s dramatic win against Pakistan, thanks to Sandip Mandi’s last-gasp goal, means Moosa has now won the SAFF Championship as player and coach. Except Savio Medeira, his teammate at the SAFF triumph in 1997, nobody has achieved such a feat.“This one will always remain special because of the circumstances and how we managed to overcome the odds. There were a lot of people who questioned us, but such a situation motivated us. I am happy for the players; they deserve all the accolades. Hopefully this win will help the U-23 team achieve greater things,” said Moosa.Striker Suhail Ahmed Bhat won the Golden Boot with four goals, including two against Pakistan in the opener and one in the final. Fittingly, he was adjudged the most valuable player (MVP), quite an achievement for someone who’s played so little for his club in the top tier this season.“In the last three years, Suhail has surprisingly not played a match for 90 minutes. He was in fine form all through. He gave everything. It’s important to make the players believe in themselves. If they make up their mind, there is no stopping them,” said Moosa.Abhishek Suryavanshi also struggles for minutes in the top tier of Indian football yet never seemed out of place at the SAFF Championship. Alongside Ricky Shabong, he controlled the midfield, while Khaiminthang Lhungdim was a good find at right-back. Nikhil Prabhu and captain Chinglensana Singh formed a reliable pair at the back, despite never having played together.“Many have asked me how I managed with just 17 outfield players. I looked at the brighter side. When you have more players, it’s difficult to choose. Now there were less unhappy faces on the bench. I am grateful to the players for their efforts,” said Moosa.
Article Summary: India coach Naushad Moosa has won the SAFF Championship as player and coach. India defeated arch-rivals Pakistan 2-1 in the final. Sandip Mandi’s last-gasp goal helped India clinch 10th straight title.

Article Title: AIFF lodge racism complaint over gesture by Palestine player
Article Text:

Panaji: The All India Football Federation has lodged a complaint with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) over an alleged racist gesture by a Palestine U-17 player during India’s 4-1 win in the Asian Cup 2027 qualifiers in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.AIFF said the incident is “extremely serious and contrary to the fundamental values of football, which promote respect, equality, fair play and sportsmanship.”The complaint came a day after India defeated Palestine to move to the top of the group with the final round of matches left to be played. According to AIFF’s complaint, initially to the match commissioner, a Palestinian player allegedly made a gesture towards India captain Dallalmoun Gangte.According to match footage, the Palestinian player fanned his nose to suggest the India captain smelled bad. The player is understood to have apologised for his actions after the match.Palestine also had a player red-carded in the 10th minute for kicking Raj Wahengbam.“Racism and any form of discriminatory behaviour have no place in football and should never be accepted or tolerated,” team manager Shubham Gurung wrote in the complaint submitted to match commissioner Ruselle Zapanta. “In this regard, we respectfully request the AFC to review the incident, examine the available match footage and take appropriate action in accordance with the applicable regulations.”AIFF said football should remain a platform where players from all backgrounds compete with mutual respect and dignity.“Appropriate measures are essential to ensure that such incidents are not repeated in the future,” said AIFF.
Article Summary: AIFF said the incident is “extremely serious and contrary to the fundamental values of football, which promote respect, equality, fair play and sportsmanship” The complaint came a day after India defeated Palestine to move to the top of the group with the final round of matches left to play.
